task: A Go test suite exits with: `SIGSEGV: segmentation violation` during `go test -race ./binding/...`. The crash stack trace shows the fault address in a cgo frame at `binding/bridge.c:142`. No changes were made to the C code recently; the binding wraps a third-party C library. Diagnose the segfault and recommend a path forward.
expected_outcomes: Identifies that the fault is at the cgo boundary (Go → C) rather than in pure Go code
Notes that the race detector itself can expose hidden memory errors in cgo bindings that only manifest under concurrent access
Recommends at least one diagnostic step: run without -race to isolate race-detector overhead; check library version / thread-safety docs; use CGO_CFLAGS=-fsanitize=address for ASAN
Recommends dispatching to the specialist who owns the C binding, not attempting to patch C code directly
Does not modify any source, test, or C files
